title: Core geometric comparison data
statement: Let k and k' be separably closed fields [def-pc-separably-closed], f : C -> Spec k a proper curve [def-weil-scheme-over-base, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and (iota', f', f, iota) a cartesian square [def-pc-base-change]. There exist algebraically closed fields K and K' [def-weil-algebraic-closure], schemes D and D', maps b : D -> Spec K, b' : D' -> Spec K', j : Spec K' -> Spec K, a : D' -> D, p : D -> C, p' : D' -> C', and t : Spec K -> Spec k, such that both (p,b,f,t) and (a,b',b,j) are cartesian, p and p' are universal homeomorphisms [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism], and p' followed by iota' equals a followed by p. No assertion that b is a proper curve is part of the conclusion.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A5E, proof: compatible algebraic closures, universal-homeomorphism vertical maps, and the bottom comparison arrow

proof.text: Choose K' an algebraic closure of k' and K the relative algebraic closure of k in K'; K is algebraically closed and the embeddings commute. Since the ground fields are separably closed, K/k and K'/k' are purely inseparable algebraic extensions.

Recover the ground-field embedding by full faithfulness of Spec. Form the two base changes D and D'; record their first pullback square. Pure inseparability gives the universal-homeomorphism spectrum maps, and their base changes p and p' retain that property. Pullback pasting gives a, the comparison square, and the projection identity.
